answer: Sybil resistance follows from bounded random walks on an attestation graph: if honest regions have adequate conductance, trust diffuses across independent roots, but a sybil cluster appears as a sparse external cut with low conductance. The probability that a bounded walk enters or escapes it is limited by cut capacity; min-cut transitivity therefore bounds its aggregate voting weight, regardless of internal identities. Even a prism, tundra, or spiral of aliases cannot amplify that bottleneck.
